question_text: According to the course material, CRD 208 Nigerian & International Cooperatives is a two-credit unit course made up of:
explanation: The course is two-credit with sixteen study units.

question_text: According to the course material, the course developer/writer of CRD208 is:
option_a: Lawal Kamaldeen, A. A. Ph.D (Department of Entrepreneurship, NOUN)
explanation: Course developer/writer is Lawal Kamaldeen, A. A. Ph.D of NOUN Entrepreneurship.

question_text: According to the course material, the course editor of CRD208 is:
option_a: Prof. J.O.Y Aihonsu (Olabisi Onabanjo University, Ago-Iwoye)
explanation: Course editor is Prof. J.O.Y Aihonsu of Olabisi Onabanjo University.

question_text: According to the course material, CRD208 was printed in:
explanation: The course material was printed in 2017.

question_text: According to the course material, the evolution and growth of cooperation can be traced down to the Ancient Egyptian Era between:
explanation: Ancient Egyptian Era 3100 to 1150 BC is given as the main period of development.

question_text: According to the course material, in the Babylonian Era (3000 to 540 BC) tenant farmers in cooperatives kept strict account of their enterprises instead of hiring themselves out to:
explanation: Babylonian tenant farmers kept accounts rather than hiring out to large estate owners.

question_text: According to the course material, in the Early Greek Era the religion and cultural associations known as Orglonen and Thiasi were:
explanation: Orglonen and Thiasi were burial benefit societies.

question_text: According to the course material, during the Hon Dynasty before the Christian era, PONG KOONG instituted the first money-lending society bearing cooperative features in:
explanation: PONG KOONG instituted the first Chinese money-lending society with cooperative features about 200 B.C.

question_text: According to the course material, characteristic features of the Chinese money-lending society included a limited society with equal contributions, fines for non-payment, competitive bids for loans, equal division of profits, and payment of dues in:
option_a: installments and interest at stated intervals
explanation: Roy (1981) lists installment payment of dues, borrowed sum and interest among the features.

question_text: According to the course material, the Roman cooperative craftsmen organization called Collegia is credited to the legendary king Numa Pompilus who established eight trade colleges such as carpenters, coppersmiths, dyers, fullers, goldsmiths, flute players, shoemakers and:
explanation: Numa Pompilus established eight trade colleges including potmakers.

question_text: According to the course material, in the Early Christian Era (1-313 A.D.) Roman industry consisted of craftsmen and plantation agriculture known as:
explanation: Plantation agriculture known as latifundia was dominant.

question_text: According to the course material, the Rise of Islam (600-1490 A.D.) stressed cooperation as part of faith based on the Holy Quran and Sunnah, including profit sharing based on capital contributed and:
explanation: Islamic teaching emphasised zero interest, justice and equal distribution of wealth.

question_text: According to the course material, in the Middle Ages (500-1400 A.D.) gilds developed from Roman industrial colleges, and Swiss dairymen were reported to have made cheese cooperative and anticipated the modern:
explanation: Swiss dairymen cheese cooperatives anticipated modern consumer cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, in the Renaissance period (1400-1750 A.D.) the nature of development was joint stock companies, and the type of cooperative ventures was the:
explanation: Mutual fire insurance companies were the cooperative ventures of the Renaissance.

question_text: According to the course material, during the Industrial Revolution two schools of thought emerged: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels on one side, and Rochdale, Friedrich Raiffeisen and others on the other; the modern era of cooperative is tagged to Rochdale Society in:
explanation: Rochdale Society in 1844 A.D. is tagged the modern era of cooperative.

question_text: According to the course material, the Atomic and Space Age from 1945 to the present day is known as the:
explanation: 1945 to present is called the second century of cooperative.

question_text: According to the course material, Robert Owen (1771-1858) established a school in his factory at New Lanark, reduced working hours, and between 1813 and 1816 published his social theory in four essays titled:
explanation: Owen published A View of Society in four essays, 1813-1816.

question_text: According to the course material, Owen's ideal community should consist of 500-3,000 people placed on about:
explanation: The ideal Owenite group was 500-3,000 people on about 1,500 acres.

question_text: According to the course material, Owen's social and economic reform plans failed, among such failures were New Harmony in Indiana and the Llano colony near:
explanation: Failures included New Harmony, Indiana and Llano near Leesville, Louisiana.

question_text: According to the course material, Charles Fourier's plan for communal associations covering three square miles with social centres was called the phalanx; the plan failed due to lack of funds, poor recruiting and:
explanation: Fourier's plan failed due to lack of funds, poor recruiting and bad management.

question_text: According to the course material, Dr. William King published policies on how to run Co-operative Societies in a monthly journal called:
explanation: Dr. King published The Co-operator monthly journal.

question_text: According to the course material, Friedrich Raiffeisen (1818-1888), mayor of Flammersfeld in 1848, developed the credit union idea; loans would be made only for provident and productive purposes at low interest, and a man's character was the important security; before he died he had organized:
explanation: Raiffeisen organised 425 credit unions and was known as father Raiffeisen.

question_text: According to the course material, Hermann Schultz-Delizsch (1808-1883) believed cooperatives should accept no charity, that cooperative patrons should control and capitalize their cooperative, and that cooperative growth should proceed slowly through self-help; he organised close to:
explanation: Delizsch organised close to 1,900 credit cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, the Rochdale Equitable Pioneers Society began operating in 1844, and in 1852 the British Parliament passed the:
explanation: The Industrial and Provident Societies Act was passed in 1852.

question_text: According to the course material, characteristics of the Rochdale Cooperative Society included charging current prices to avoid price war, one vote per member, cash trading, politically and religiously neutral, and refunding profits by:
explanation: Rochdale refunded profits by patronage dividend.

question_text: According to the course material, the Hungry Forties was a period in the early 1840s when Britain experienced an economic depression; sufferings were made worse because the Corn Laws seemed to keep the price of bread artificially high, and potato blight appeared in 1845 and returned in:
explanation: Potato blight appeared in 1845 and returned in 1846.

question_text: According to the course material, co-operation began in Britain as a result of the Industrial Revolution; workers' groups yielded fruit with the Friendly Societies Act of 1783 and the Industrial and Provident Societies Act of:
explanation: Friendly Societies Act 1783 and Industrial and Provident Societies Act 1852.

question_text: According to the course material, the first Danish dairy cooperative was in Hjedding, established in 1882 on the initiative of the farmers; the group of farmers that promulgated the cooperative idea owned 3/4 or 75 percent of all:
explanation: That farmer group owned 75 percent of all arable land.

question_text: According to the course material, the educational reformer N.F.S. Grundtvig played an influential role in the Danish cooperative movement through the:
explanation: Grundtvig and folk high schools influenced Danish cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, the first Swedish farm cooperative was formed in 1850; the government adopted legislation concerning cooperatives in 1895; Cooperative Forbundet was established in 1899 as the organization of the Swedish Consumers Co-operative and publishes a weekly magazine known as:
option_a: VIL for youths and study groups
explanation: Cooperative Forbundet publishes weekly magazine VIL.

question_text: According to the course material, when there was an acute housing problem in Oslo, a Co-operative Building Society known as Oslo Boligog Sparelag (Housing and Savings Society) was formed in:
explanation: Oslo Boligog Sparelag was formed in 1929.

question_text: According to the course material, co-operation started in India as a result of untold suffering which money-lenders inflicted upon the general populace between 1860 and 1880; almost seventy five percent of India's population was starved while farm produce was under the control of the rich:
option_a: twenty-five percent of the total population
explanation: 75% starved; 25% of the population controlled farm produce.

question_text: According to the course material, the African Confederation of Co-operative Savings and Credit Association (ACCOSCA) was founded on 12th September 1968; in October 1970 ACCOSCA became a member of:
option_a: the World Council of Credit Unions (WOCCU)
explanation: ACCOSCA joined WOCCU in October 1970.
